description:
A French manuscript copy of a lost Russian map of Siberia, probably compiled between 1675 and 1685, from the Cartes Marines collection of French colonial maps. Its full title promises “all the rivers, towns and streams, and the dwellings of the Tartars and Kalmyks”: the Russian names are written in French spelling, and tents mark the nomadic peoples, from the Yakuts and Tungus to the Kalmyks, Bashkirs and Mongols, down to the Great Wall and Peking.
Every text on it was read from the scan by an AI model, Claude Opus 5.5, working in four parts: 55 titles, notes and names of peoples and regions, pinned on the map, and 264 towns, rivers and lakes, shown when you choose them in the filter. No published transcription exists, so the readings are the model's, with its own confidence for each. The labels along the lines between the four parts were read a second time, independently: 48 of 73 agree letter for letter, and the 25 that differ, almost all small river names, are flagged in their commentary as worth checking.
The scan is faded, so the map view has its contrast adjusted to bring out pale ink; “As scanned” shows the Newberry image itself.
